Battery recycling capacity doubles in three years

Battery recycling capacity has doubled over the past three years as several new plants opened and older facilities expanded. Industry analysts expect the trend to continue while electric-vehicle adoption grows and used packs reach the end of their first life.

The report finds that recovered lithium, nickel and cobalt volumes are still small compared with demand, but the direction is clear. Recycling groups say collection networks, not processing capacity, are now the main bottleneck in most markets.

Regulators are drafting clearer rules for battery passports and for the traceability of recovered materials, which the industry says will help buyers compare suppliers on a consistent basis.
